inputs.root_cause: Event 327's own exact_next_action named per-format obligation closure as the mission's own next dominant activity now that all six formats are gate-complete. Surveyed nrrd's own 14 remaining obligations directly rather than assuming scope from prior framing. NRRD-CONVERT-001 (SAL-NRRD-OBL-E2B0331E7D4F6AD8) stood out: its own missing_behavior was a single, precisely-scoped sentence ('Scaling (as opposed to clipping/rounding) is not implemented for dtype conversion: no explicit scale-factor parameter exists yet'), and a prior evidence entry (NRRD-ATTACHMENT-CONVERSION-PROOF, Event 316) had already explicitly flagged this as the ONE remaining quarter of a four-part compound obligation, having already closed the other three (dtype/endian at baseline, encoding at Event 300, attached/detached form at Event 316 itself).
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-NRRD-OBL-E2B0331E7D4F6AD8 (NRRD-CONVERT-001) promoted partial -> implemented, closing the obligation's own last named policy.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: Read convert_dtype()'s own current implementation directly: it already has a well-established, no-default-allowed policy pattern (OverflowPolicy, RoundingPolicy) that a scale parameter slots into naturally. Added scale: float | None = None, applied to every value before overflow/rounding are evaluated. Widened the existing float-source-requires-rounding guard to also require rounding when scale is given to an integer target (a non-integer scale factor can introduce fractional values even from an integer source, e.g. 10 * 0.5 = 5.0 exactly but 10 * 0.3 = 3.0000000000000004 in float arithmetic -- the guard is conservative and static, not per-value, matching the same philosophy the existing source_is_float check already uses). scale defaults to None with byte-for-byte identical behavior to before (a dedicated regression test proves this), so the change is purely additive.
inputs.regression_tier: nrrd suite plus 6-format regression, mypy --strict, ruff

execution_steps: 1. Listed all 14 of nrrd's own remaining non-implemented obligations directly from shared/format-contracts/implementation-evidence/nrrd.yaml rather than trusting any prior summary. Read each one's own missing_behavior text: NRRD-PAYLOAD-001 (a deliberate security refusal, not a gap), NRRD-WRITE-001 ('no detached partition writer or complete conditional/optional absence policy' -- ambiguous scope, possibly overlapping with already-closed attachment-conversion work, needs deeper investigation), NRRD-ENC-001 (a large exhaustive-matrix/oracle undertaking), NRRD-SPACE-001 partial (needs real DICOM-derived test data this repo does not have), NRRD-HEADER-001 (already investigated twice, genuinely ambiguous per its own prior note), NRRD-SHAPE-001 (a first-class axis-order model, likely sizeable), NRRD-PRESERVE-001 (typed-defaults modeling, uncertain size), NRRD-CONVERT-001 (a single, precisely-named missing policy), NRRD-ARRAY-001 x2 (a full numpy-like array/slicing/view API, clearly large).

2. NRRD-CONVERT-001 stood out as the most precisely scoped: its own missing_behavior was one sentence naming exactly one thing (a scale-factor parameter), and a prior evidence entry from earlier this session (NRRD-ATTACHMENT-CONVERSION-PROOF, Event 316) had already explicitly and honestly flagged scaling as the deliberately-not-attempted final quarter of this same four-part obligation.

3. Read convert_dtype()'s own current signature and body directly (src/python/nrrd/src/format_factory/nrrd/convert.py) -- confirmed the existing OverflowPolicy/RoundingPolicy pattern (explicit, no defaults, a ConversionReport recording what happened) was a natural, small extension point for a scale parameter, not a separate conversion pathway.

4. Added scale: float | None = None to convert_dtype()'s own signature, applied via `working = working * scale` immediately after establishing `working = value`, before any rounding/clipping logic. Added a matching scale: float | None = None field to ConversionReport.

5. Widened the existing validation guard: `target_is_integer and source_is_float and rounding is None: raise` became `target_is_integer and may_be_non_integral and rounding is None: raise`, where `may_be_non_integral = source_is_float or scale is not None` -- a non-integer scale factor can introduce fractional values even from an integer source, so the same explicit-rounding requirement a float source already has now also applies when scaling is used.
6. Ran mypy --strict and ruff on the changed file -- clean, zero issues, zero ignores needed.

7. Ran the pre-existing 13-test test_obligation_dtype_conversion.py file BEFORE writing any new test, to confirm zero regression from the signature change (all default parameters, purely additive) -- 13/13 passed unchanged.

8. Added 5 new tests: a normalized [0,1]->[0,255] uint8 remap (with an honestly-reasoned is_lossless=False assertion, since 0.5*255=127.5 is genuinely fractional and gets rounded, not silently treated as exact), an out-of-range-after-scaling clip case, the integer-source-non-integer-scale rounding-required refusal, a working integer-source-scaled-and-rounded success case, and a dedicated no-scale-given-is-byte-for-byte-unchanged regression proof. One initial test assertion was wrong on first write (expected is_lossless=True for a case that actually required rounding) -- caught by running the test, not assumed correct; fixed the assertion, not the code, since the code's own behavior (correctly reporting a genuinely fractional intermediate value as rounded) was right.
9. Ran the full nrrd suite (680 passed, 1 skipped, was 675) and the 6-format regression to confirm zero collateral impact.

10. Updated the ledger: promoted SAL-NRRD-OBL-E2B0331E7D4F6AD8 to status=implemented (missing_behavior: []), added the 4 new positive test selectors and 1 new negative test selector, added a new execution_evidence entry (NRRD-DTYPE-SCALE-CONVERSION-PROOF), and corrected NRRD-ATTACHMENT-CONVERSION-PROOF's own prior truth_boundary text (which had explicitly said scaling was NOT resolved by that entry) to point at this new entry as the one that closed it, rather than leaving a now-stale claim standing.
